eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
title: Trained DBP-X: width of the Kerr window R = 1, 3, 7, 15 at Ns = 8 and 20
question: How much BER reduction does trained DBP-X gain from the memory of the Kerr phase (window R = 3, 7, 15 against the instantaneous R = 1) at Ns = 8 and 20, and at what cost?
model: dbpx.DBPX trained by dbpx.train_one without changes: D_total exact and fixed; Ns steps [symmetric FIR L = 255 by circular FFT, Kerr phase with symmetric alpha of R taps]; complex output gain
start: physical taps (L = 255); alpha = g * delta / (Ns * P) (classical kernel: the same start for every R, memory only by training); sign, multiplier and g of the E050 start choice for classical (start_best.csv, validation): Ns 8: sign +1, mult 0.85, g 0.16; Ns 20: sign +1, mult 1.05, g 0.38
training: two stages as the best E050 arm: L_D (Xiao) 3000 iterations Adam 1e-3 (lowest L_D kept), then MSE Adam 1e-4, 5000 iterations, 4 whole train files per iteration with a random circular shift; checkpoint with the minimum validation MSE (every 100 iterations), test reported there
reproduction: Ns 20, R 7 repeats the E050 arm 'classical, two' (99.249 %, 10 seeds; same seeds 17-71 among them): difference within 2 SE expected
rm: dbpx.rm_columns (project, xiao, merged) and e054_prune.rm_both (direct and FFT, 4 and 3 RM per complex product), D_total 401 taps; the RM convention is not changed (pending advisor)
notes: Ns 8 at L = 255 was not in the E050 truncation unit test (only Ns 20, 40); the step memory at Ns 8 is about 34 symbols, far below 255
the cost is dominated by the FIR of 255 taps: R changes the RM by less than 2 % in the direct convention

rule_draft.memory_helps: at a given Ns, R > 1 is better than R = 1 if test(R) - test(1) > 2 SE and > 2 std (5 seeds); otherwise 'not proven'
rule_draft.sufficient_R: the smallest R whose mean is within max(2 SE, 2 std) of the best R at that Ns
rule_draft.report: mean, std, SE, range over seeds; RM in all columns; plateau iteration
rule_draft.limits: one schedule, no tuning of the schedule or of g per R; 5 seeds; circular files; one channel, one polarization, 1 sps

value_filter.changes_next_step: yes: whether the Kerr memory is worth its cost in DBP-X or R = 1 suffices
value_filter.needed_for_main_claim: yes: E016/E056 showed Kerr memory helps the closed-form models; not checked for trained DBP-X
